units.zh: 張全義
units.en: Zhang Quanyi
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi

units.zh: 張全義，字國維，濮州臨濮人也。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi, styled Guowei, came from Linpu in Puzhou.
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi, courtesy name Guowei, was a native of Linpu in Puzhou.

units.zh: 少以田家子役於縣，縣令數困辱之，全義因亡入黃巢賊中。
units.en: As a boy he did corvée for the county as a farmer’s son. The magistrate shamed him again and again; Quanyi ran off and joined Huang Chao’s rebels.
units.literal: In youth, as a farmer’s son, he served corvée for the county; the magistrate repeatedly humiliated him, and Quanyi therefore fled into Huang Chao’s band.

units.zh: 巢陷長安，以全義為吏部尚書、水運使。
units.en: When Chao seized Chang’an he made Quanyi Minister of the Civil Service and commissioner of water transport.
units.literal: When Chao took Chang’an, he made Quanyi Minister of the Civil Service and transport commissioner for waterways.

units.zh: 巢賊敗，去事諸葛爽於河陽。
units.en: After Chao’s fall he went to Zhuge Shuang at Heyang.
units.literal: When Chao’s rebels were defeated, he left to serve Zhuge Shuang at Heyang.

units.zh: 爽死，事其子仲方。
units.en: Shuang died; he served the son Zhongfang.
units.literal: When Shuang died, he served his son Zhongfang.

units.zh: 仲方為孫儒所逐，全義與李罕之分據河陽、洛陽以附於梁，二人相得甚歡。
units.en: Sun Ru drove out Zhongfang. Quanyi and Li Hanzhi split Heyang and Luoyang and came over to Liang. The two were fast friends.
units.literal: Zhongfang was driven out by Sun Ru; Quanyi and Li Hanzhi divided Heyang and Luoyang between them and submitted to Liang, and the two men were very pleased with each other.

units.zh: 然罕之性貪暴，日以寇鈔為事。
units.en: Hanzhi was greedy and brutal; every day was for raiding and loot.
units.literal: Yet Hanzhi’s nature was greedy and violent; day by day he made raiding and plunder his business.

units.zh: 全義勤儉，禦軍有法，督民耕殖。
units.en: Quanyi was thrifty, kept strict discipline in camp, and drove the people back to the fields.
units.literal: Quanyi was diligent and frugal, governed the army by rule, and urged the people to till and plant.

units.zh: 以故，罕之常乏食，而全義常有餘。
units.en: So Hanzhi went hungry while Quanyi’s granaries stayed full.
units.literal: For this reason Hanzhi often lacked food, while Quanyi often had surplus.

units.zh: 罕之仰給全義，全義不能給，二人因有隙。
units.en: Hanzhi lived on Quanyi’s grain until Quanyi could give no more; then the friendship cracked.
units.literal: Hanzhi looked to Quanyi for support; Quanyi could not supply him, and the two therefore had a rift.

units.zh: 罕之出兵攻晉、絳，全義襲取河陽，罕之奔晉，晉遣兵助罕之，圍全義甚急。
units.en: Hanzhi marched against Jin and Jiang Prefectures. Quanyi struck behind him and seized Heyang. Hanzhi fled to Jin, whose troops came to his aid and pressed Quanyi hard in siege.
units.literal: Hanzhi led troops to attack Jin Prefecture and Jiang Prefecture; Quanyi seized Heyang in a surprise attack; Hanzhi fled to Jin, which sent troops to aid him and press Quanyi hard in siege.

units.zh: 全義乞兵於梁，梁遣牛存節、丁會等以兵萬人自九鼎渡河，擊敗罕之於沇水，晉軍解去。
units.en: Quanyi cried to Liang for men. Niu Cunjie and Ding Hui crossed at Jiuding with ten thousand troops, smashed Hanzhi on the Yan River, and Jin pulled away.
units.literal: Quanyi begged troops from Liang; Liang sent Niu Cunjie, Ding Hui, and others with ten thousand men to cross the river at Jiuding, defeated Hanzhi on the Yan River, and the Jin army withdrew.

units.zh: 梁以丁會守河陽，全義還為河南尹。
units.en: Liang left Ding Hui in Heyang; Quanyi resumed as Intendant of Henan.
units.literal: Liang had Ding Hui hold Heyang; Quanyi returned to be Henan Intendant.

units.zh: 全義德梁出己，由是盡心焉。
units.en: Liang had pulled him out of the fire; Quanyi served with all he had.
units.literal: Quanyi was grateful to Liang for saving him and therefore gave it his whole heart.

units.zh: 是時，河南遭巢、儒兵火之後，城邑殘破，戶不滿百，全義披荊棘，勸耕殖，躬載酒食，勞民畎畝之間，築南、北二城以居之。
units.en: Chao and Ru had burned Henan hollow—fewer than a hundred households left. Quanyi cut brush, pushed the plow, carried wine and food into the furrows himself, and raised south and north cities for people to live in.
units.literal: At that time, after the fires of Chao’s and Ru’s armies, Henan’s walls lay in ruins and households numbered fewer than a hundred. Quanyi cleared the thorns, urged farming, himself carried wine and food to labor among the fields, and built southern and northern cities for the people to dwell in.

units.zh: 數年，人物完盛，民甚賴之。
units.en: In a few years the land filled out again; the people leaned on him.
units.literal: Within several years people and things flourished again, and the common folk relied on him greatly.

units.zh: 及梁太祖劫唐昭宗東遷，繕理宮闕、府廨、倉庫，皆全義之力也。
units.en: When Zhu Wen dragged Zhaozong east, every palace, yamen, and warehouse put back in order was Quanyi’s work.
units.literal: When Liang Taizu seized Tang’s Emperor Zhaozong and moved him east, the repair of palaces, government offices, and storehouses was all Quanyi’s doing.

units.zh: 全義初名言，唐昭宗賜名全義。
units.en: He had first been called Yan; Zhaozong gave him the name Quanyi—“whole righteousness.”
units.literal: Quanyi had first been named Yan; Emperor Zhaozong bestowed the name Quanyi.

units.zh: 唐亡，全義事梁，又請改名，太祖賜名宗奭。
units.en: Tang ended; he served Liang and asked for a new name. The Founder called him Zongshi.
units.literal: When Tang fell, Quanyi served Liang and again asked to change his name; the Founder bestowed the name Zongshi.

units.zh: 太祖猜忌，晚年尤甚，全義奉事益謹，卒以自免。
units.en: Zhu Wen grew more suspicious with age; Quanyi bowed lower year by year and lived.
units.literal: The Founder was suspicious by nature, and in his later years especially so; Quanyi served all the more carefully and in the end escaped harm.

units.zh: 自梁與晉戰河北，兵數敗亡，全義輒搜卒伍鎧馬，月獻之以補其缺。
units.en: While Liang and Jin tore at Hebei and Liang’s hosts bled men and horses, Quanyi combed his camps every month for mail and mounts to send north and patch the holes.
units.literal: From the time Liang and Jin fought in Hebei and Liang’s armies suffered repeated defeat and loss, Quanyi would search the ranks for armor and horses and each month present them to fill the gaps.

units.zh: 太祖兵敗蓚縣，道病，還洛，幸全義會節園避暑，留旬日，全義妻女皆迫淫之。
units.en: After his army was defeated at Tiao County, Zhu Wen fell ill on the road back to Luoyang. He spent ten days escaping the summer heat at Quanyi's Festival Garden, where he forced Quanyi's wife and daughters to submit to him.
units.literal: When the Founder’s army was defeated at Tiao County, he fell ill on the road and returned to Luoyang. He visited Quanyi’s Festival Garden to escape the summer heat and stayed ten days; Quanyi’s wife and daughters were all forced to submit to him.

units.zh: 其子繼祚憤恥不自勝，欲剚刃太祖，全義止之曰：「吾為李罕之兵圍河陽，啖木屑以為食，惟有一馬，欲殺以餉軍，死在朝夕，而梁兵擊之，得至今日，此恩不可忘也。」
units.en: His son Jizu burned with shame and reached for a knife. Quanyi caught his arm: “Hanzhi had me penned at Heyang eating sawdust. One horse left—I meant to slaughter it for the men. I was as good as dead when Liang broke the siege. Do not forget that debt.”
units.literal: His son Jizu, shamed and furious beyond bearing, wished to draw a blade on the Founder; Quanyi stopped him and said: “When Li Hanzhi’s troops besieged me at Heyang we ate sawdust for food; I had but one horse and meant to kill it to feed the army; death was at hand morning and night—and Liang’s soldiers struck and I reached today. That kindness must not be forgotten.”

units.zh: 繼祚乃止。
units.en: Jizu laid the blade down.
units.literal: Jizu then stopped.

units.zh: 嘗有言全義於太祖者，太祖召全義，其意不測。
units.en: Word reached Zhu Wen that Quanyi was not to be trusted. He summoned him—you could not read his face.
units.literal: Once someone spoke against Quanyi to the Founder; the Founder summoned Quanyi, his intent unknowable.

units.zh: 全義妻儲氏明敏有口辯，遽入見，厲聲曰：「宗奭，種田叟爾！
units.en: His wife Lady Chu was quick and had a tongue like a blade. She went straight in and snapped: “Zongshi? A dirt farmer, nothing more!
units.literal: Quanyi’s wife, Lady Chu, was clever and sharp-tongued; she rushed in to see him and said in a fierce voice: “Zongshi is nothing but an old farmer!

units.zh: 守河南三十年，開荒斫土，捃拾財賦，助陛下創業，今年齒衰朽，已無能為，而陛下疑之，何也？」
units.en: Thirty years he has kept Henan—cut brush, broke ground, scraped every tax to feed your founding. His bones are old and useless, and you doubt him. For what?”
units.literal: For thirty years he has held Henan, cleared wilderness, hewed soil, gathered taxes and levies, and helped Your Majesty build the enterprise—and now his teeth are rotten and he can do nothing, yet Your Majesty doubts him. Why?”

units.zh: 太祖笑曰：「我無惡心，嫗勿多言。」
units.en: The Founder laughed: “No harm meant, old mother—enough talk.”
units.literal: The Founder laughed and said: “I bear no ill will; old woman, speak no more.”

units.zh: 全義事梁，累拜中書令，食邑至萬三千戶，兼領忠武陜虢鄭滑河陽節度使、判六軍諸衛事、天下兵馬副元帥，封魏王。
units.en: He rose to Grand Councilor, thirteen thousand households, and at once Zhongwu, Shaan, Guo, Zheng, Hua, and Heyang; he judged the Six Armies and palace guards, stood second only to the commander-in-chief, and was made Prince of Wei.
units.literal: Quanyi served Liang, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Councilor, with a fief of thirteen thousand households, and concurrently held the circuits of Zhongwu, Shaan, Guo, Zheng, Hua, and Heyang, judged the Six Armies and palace guards, was vice commander-in-chief of all armed forces under Heaven, and was enfeoffed Prince of Wei.

units.zh: 初，全義為李罕之所敗，其弟全武及其家屬為晉兵所得，晉王給以田宅，待之甚厚，全義常陰遣人通問於太原。
units.en: When Hanzhi beat him once, his brother Quanwu and kin fell to Jin. Li Keyong gave them land and kept them well. Quanyi still sent quiet word to Taiyuan.
units.literal: Earlier, when Quanyi was defeated by Li Hanzhi, his younger brother Quanwu and his household were taken by Jin troops; the Prince of Jin gave them fields and houses and treated them very generously; Quanyi often sent men in secret to inquire at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 及梁亡，莊宗入汴，全義自洛來朝，泥首待罪，莊宗勞之曰：「卿家弟侄，幸復相見。」
units.en: Liang died; Zhuangzong took Bian. Quanyi came from Luoyang, face in the dust, ready for death. Zhuangzong raised him: “Your brothers and nephews—good to see them whole again.”
units.literal: When Liang fell, Zhuangzong entered Bian; Quanyi came from Luoyang to court, smeared his head in the dust and awaited punishment; Zhuangzong comforted him, saying: “Your family’s younger brothers and nephews—it is fortunate we can meet again.”

units.zh: 全義俯伏感涕。
units.en: Quanyi pressed his forehead to the floor and wept.
units.literal: Quanyi prostrated himself, weeping with gratitude.

units.zh: 年老不能進趨，遣人掖扶而登，宴犒盡歡，命皇子繼岌、皇弟存紀等皆兄事之。
units.en: Too old to hurry, he was helped up the steps. The feast ran late. Zhuangzong told Jiji, Cunji, and the rest to honor him as elder brother.
units.literal: Old and unable to hurry forward, he had men support him by the arms to ascend; at the feast they drank to the full; he ordered the princes Jiji and the emperor’s younger brother Cunji and others all to treat him as an elder brother.

units.zh: 全義因去梁所賜名，請復其故名。
units.en: He dropped the Liang name and asked for his old one back.
units.literal: Quanyi therefore cast off the name Liang had given and asked to restore his former name.

units.zh: 而全義猶不自安，乃厚賂劉皇后以自托。
units.en: Still he could not rest easy and bought Empress Liu with heavy gifts.
units.literal: Yet Quanyi still was not at ease and therefore bribed Empress Liu heavily to secure himself.

units.zh: 初，梁末帝幸洛陽，將祀天於南郊而不果，其儀仗法物猶在，全義因請幸洛陽，白南郊儀物已具。
units.en: Liang’s Last Emperor had come to Luoyang for the southern-suburb rite and failed; the gear was still there. Quanyi asked Zhuangzong to come, swearing the suburban vessels were waiting.
units.literal: Earlier, when Liang’s Last Emperor visited Luoyang and meant to sacrifice to Heaven at the southern suburb but did not succeed, the ritual regalia and implements remained; Quanyi therefore asked that Zhuangzong visit Luoyang and reported that the southern-suburb ritual objects were ready.

units.zh: 莊宗大悅，加拜全義太師、尚書令。
units.en: Zhuangzong was delighted and made him Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was greatly pleased and promoted Quanyi to Grand Preceptor and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 明年十一月，莊宗幸洛陽，南郊而禮物不具，因改用來年二月，然不以前語責全義。
units.en: Next year, eleventh month, he reached Luoyang. The suburban gifts were not ready; the rite slid to second month next year—and he never called Quanyi to account for the lie.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the next year Zhuangzong visited Luoyang; the southern-suburb gifts were not ready, so the rite was moved to the second month of the coming year, yet he did not blame Quanyi for his earlier words.

units.zh: 以皇后故，待之愈厚，數幸其第，命皇后拜全義為父，改封齊王。
units.en: For the empress’s sake his favor deepened. Zhuangzong came to his house again and again, had the empress call him father, and changed his title to Prince of Qi.
units.literal: Because of the empress he treated him all the more generously, visited his mansion many times, ordered the empress to acknowledge Quanyi as father, and changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Qi.

units.zh: 初，莊宗滅梁，欲掘梁太祖墓，斫棺戮屍。
units.en: When he destroyed Liang he meant to open Zhu Wen’s tomb, break the coffin, and mutilate the body.
units.literal: Earlier, when Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, he wished to dig up Liang Taizu’s tomb, split the coffin, and hack the corpse.

units.zh: 全義以謂梁雖仇敵，今已屠滅其家，足以報怨，剖棺之戮，非王者以大度示天下也。
units.en: Quanyi argued that Liang was your foe, but the clan was wiped out—that paid the debt. A king does not show the world his spite by gutting a grave.
units.literal: Quanyi held that though Liang was an enemy, its house was already slaughtered to the last—enough to repay the grudge—and that disemboweling a tomb was not how a king shows magnanimity to the world.

units.zh: 莊宗以為然，鏟去墓闕而已。
units.en: Zhuangzong agreed and only stripped the tomb’s stone tower.
units.literal: Zhuangzong thought it right and merely scraped away the tomb’s spirit tower.

units.zh: 全義監軍嘗得李德裕平泉醒酒石，德裕孫延古，因托全義復求之。
units.en: His army supervisor had taken Li Deyu’s Pingquan sobering stone. Deyu’s grandson Yan’gu asked Quanyi to get it back.
units.literal: Quanyi’s army supervisor once obtained Li Deyu’s Pingquan sobering stone; Deyu’s grandson Yan’gu, trusting Quanyi, asked him to recover it.

units.zh: 監軍忿然曰：「自黃巢亂後，洛陽園宅無復能守，豈獨平泉一石哉！」
units.en: The supervisor snarled: “Since Chao, not one Luoyang estate could be held—why fuss over one Pingquan stone!”
units.literal: The supervisor said angrily: “Since the Huang Chao turmoil, no garden or mansion in Luoyang could be kept—how is Pingquan alone a single stone!”

units.zh: 全義嘗在巢賊中，以為譏己，固大怒，奏笞殺監軍者，天下冤之。
units.en: Quanyi had ridden with Chao once and heard an insult. He raged, had the man flogged to death, and the realm cried foul.
units.literal: Quanyi had once been in Chao’s band and took it as a barb at himself; he was therefore furious and memorialized that the supervisor be beaten to death; the empire thought it unjust.

units.zh: 其聽訟，以先訴者為直，民頗以為苦。
units.en: In court he favored whoever filed first; folk groaned under it.
units.literal: In hearing lawsuits he took whoever sued first as in the right; the people found it hard to bear.

units.zh: 同光四年，趙在禮反於魏，元行欽討賊無功，莊宗欲自將討之，大臣皆諫以為不可，因言明宗可將。
units.en: Tongguang 4: Zhao Zaili rose in Wei. Yuan Xingqin could not break him. Zhuangzong meant to go himself; ministers begged him not to and named Mingzong instead.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tongguang, Zhao Zaili rebelled at Wei; Yuan Xingqin campaigned against the rebels without success; Zhuangzong wished to lead the army himself; the great ministers all remonstrated that he should not; they therefore said Mingzong could command.

units.zh: 是時，郭崇韜、朱友謙皆已見殺，明宗自鎮州來朝，處之私第，莊宗疑之，不欲遣也。
units.en: Guo Chongtao and Zhu Youqian were already dead. Mingzong came from Zhenzhou and was kept in a private house. Zhuangzong mistrusted him and would not send him out.
units.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao and Zhu Youqian had already been killed; Mingzong came from Zhenzhou to court and was lodged in a private residence; Zhuangzong suspected him and did not wish to send him.

units.zh: 群臣固請，不從；
units.en: Ministers pressed again and again; he refused;
units.literal: The ministers pressed their plea repeatedly; he would not heed them;

units.zh: 最後全義力以為言，莊宗乃從。
units.en: only when Quanyi spoke hard for it did Zhuangzong yield.
units.literal: only at the last did Quanyi speak forcefully for it, and Zhuangzong then consented.

units.zh: 已而明宗至魏果反，全義以憂卒，年七十五，謚曰忠肅。
units.en: Mingzong reached Wei and turned rebel. Quanyi died of grief at seventy-five. They styled him Loyal and Solemn.
units.literal: Before long Mingzong reached Wei and indeed rebelled; Quanyi died of grief, aged seventy-five; his posthumous title was Loyal and Solemn.

units.zh: 子繼祚，官至上將軍。
units.en: His son Jizu rose to supreme general.
units.literal: His son Jizu rose to the post of supreme general.

units.zh: 晉高祖時，與張從賓反於河陽，當族誅。
units.en: Under Jin’s Gaozu he followed Zhang Congbin’s revolt at Heyang and earned extinction for his line.
units.literal: In the time of Jin’s Gaozu, he joined Zhang Congbin in rebellion at Heyang and was due for clan extermination.

units.zh: 而宰相桑維翰以其父珙嘗事全義有恩，乞全活之，不許，止誅繼祚及其妻子而已。
units.en: Chancellor Sang Weihan’s father Gong had served Quanyi well; he begged mercy for the clan. Denied—but only Jizu, his wife, and children died.
units.literal: But Chancellor Sang Weihan, because his father Gong had once served Quanyi with kindness, begged that the whole clan be spared; it was not granted—only Jizu and his wife and children were put to death.

units.zh: 朱友謙
units.en: Zhu Youqian
units.literal: Zhu Youqian

units.zh: 朱友謙，字德光，許州人也。
units.en: Zhu Youqian, styled Deguang, came from Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhu Youqian, courtesy name Deguang, was a native of Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 初名簡，以卒隸澠池鎮，有罪亡去，為盜石濠、三鄉之間，商旅行路皆苦之。
units.en: First he was Jian—a soldier at Mianchi, then a fugitive. He robbed between Shihao and Sanxiang until every merchant on the road feared him.
units.literal: He was first named Jian; as a soldier he was enrolled at Mianchi garrison, committed a crime and fled, and became a bandit between Shihao and Sanxiang; merchants on the road all suffered from him.

units.zh: 久之，去，為陜州軍校。
units.en: In time he left the hills for a post in the Shaan garrison.
units.literal: After a long while he left and became an officer in the Shaan army.

units.zh: 陜州節度使王珙，為人嚴酷，與其弟珂爭河中，戰敗，其牙將李璠與友謙謀，共殺珙，附於梁，太祖表璠代珙。
units.en: Wang Gong of Shaan was cruel; he and his brother Ke fought for Hezhong and lost. His yamen officer Li Fan and Youqian killed Gong and came to Liang. Zhu Wen named Fan to replace him.
units.literal: The Shaan military commissioner Wang Gong was harsh by nature; he and his younger brother Ke fought over Hezhong, was defeated in battle, and his yamen officer Li Fan plotted with Youqian, together killed Gong, and submitted to Liang; the Founder memorialized Fan to replace Gong.

units.zh: 璠立，友謙復以兵攻之，璠得逃去，梁太祖又表友謙代璠。
units.en: Fan took the seat; Youqian attacked again. Fan ran. Zhu Wen put Youqian in his place.
units.literal: When Fan was installed, Youqian again attacked him with troops; Fan escaped; Liang Taizu again memorialized Youqian to replace Fan.

units.zh: 梁兵西攻李茂貞，太祖往來過陜，友謙奉事尤謹，因請曰：「仆本無功，而富貴至此，元帥之力也。
units.en: Liang marched west on Li Maozhen; the Founder passed through Shaan again and again. Youqian waited on him like a shadow and said: “I had no merit. Everything I am, Marshal, is your doing.
units.literal: When Liang’s army campaigned west against Li Maozhen, the Founder came and went through Shaan; Youqian served with extreme care and therefore requested: “I originally had no merit, yet wealth and honor to this point—all the Marshal’s power.

units.zh: 且幸同姓，願更名以齒諸子。」
units.en: We even share the Zhu name—I beg a new name to stand among your sons.”
units.literal: Moreover we are fortunate to share a surname; I wish to change my name to rank with your sons.”

units.zh: 太祖益憐之，乃更其名友謙，錄以為子。
units.en: Zhu Wen’s heart softened; he renamed him Youqian and took him as a son.
units.literal: The Founder pitied him all the more, changed his name to Youqian, and enrolled him as a son.

units.zh: 太祖即位，徙鎮河中，累遷中書令，封冀王。
units.en: At the founding he was moved to Hezhong, rose to Grand Councilor, and was made Prince of Ji.
units.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Youqian was transferred to hold Hezhong, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Councilor, and was enfeoffed Prince of Ji.

units.zh: 太祖遇弒，友珪立，加友謙侍中，友謙雖受命，而心常不平。
units.en: Zhu Wen was murdered; Yougui seized the throne and made Youqian Palace Attendant. He took the seal but never made peace with it.
units.literal: When the Founder was assassinated, Yougui took the throne and added Youqian as Palace Attendant; though Youqian accepted the appointment, in his heart he was always ill at ease.

units.zh: 已而友珪使召友謙入覲，友謙不行，乃附於晉。
units.en: Yougui called him to court; Youqian stayed away and went over to Jin.
units.literal: Before long Yougui sent to summon Youqian to court; Youqian would not go and therefore submitted to Jin.

units.zh: 友珪遣招討使韓將康懷英等兵五萬擊友謙。
units.en: Yougui sent Kang Huaiying and fifty thousand men against him.
units.literal: Yougui sent the campaign commissioner Kang Huaiying and others with fifty thousand men to attack Youqian.

units.zh: 晉王出澤、潞以救之，遇懷英於解縣，大敗之，追至白逕嶺，夜秉炬擊之，懷英又敗，梁兵乃解去。
units.en: The Prince of Jin came from Ze and Lu to rescue him. He met Huaiying at Jie County and routed him, pursued him to Baijing Ridge, and attacked by torchlight at night. Huaiying was defeated again, and the Liang army withdrew.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin marched out from Ze and Lu to rescue him, met Huaiying at Jie county, utterly defeated him, pursued to Baijing Ridge, struck him again at night with torches, and Huaiying was defeated again; the Liang army then withdrew.

units.zh: 友謙醉寢晉王帳中，晉王視之，顧左右曰：「冀王雖甚貴，然恨其臂短耳！」
units.en: Youqian fell asleep drunk in the Prince of Jin's tent. The prince looked him over and said to his attendants, 'The Prince of Ji may be very exalted, but unfortunately his arms are short!'
units.literal: Youqian, drunk, slept in the Prince of Jin’s tent; the Prince of Jin looked at him and said to those beside him: “Though the Prince of Ji is most exalted, I regret that his arms are short!”

units.zh: 莊宗滅梁入洛，友謙來朝，賜姓名曰李繼麟，賜予巨萬。
units.en: Zhuangzong took Luoyang; Youqian came to court. He was given the Li surname and the name Jilin and gifts beyond counting.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and entered Luoyang, Youqian came to court; he was bestowed the surname Li and the name Jilin, and gifts in the tens of thousands.

units.zh: 明年，加守太師、尚書令，賜鐵券恕死罪。
units.en: Next year: acting Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and an iron pardon for death.
units.literal: The next year he was further made acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Imperial Secretariat and granted an iron certificate forgiving capital crimes.

units.zh: 以其子令德為遂州節度使，令錫忠武軍節度使，諸子及其將校為刺史者十餘人，恩寵之盛，時無與比。
units.en: Son Lingde took Suizhou; Lingxi took Zhongwu; more than ten sons and officers held prefectures—no favor like it in the age.
units.literal: His son Lingde was made military commissioner of Suizhou, Lingxi military commissioner of Zhongwu, and his sons and their commanders as prefects numbered more than ten—favor such as none could match in that age.

units.zh: 是時宦官、伶人用事，多求賂於友謙，友謙不能給而辭焉，宦官、伶人皆怒。
units.en: Eunuchs and actors ruled the court and shook Youqian down. He could not pay and said no. They hated him for it.
units.literal: At that time eunuchs and actor-favorites held power and often demanded bribes from Youqian; Youqian could not pay and declined; eunuchs and actors were all angry.

units.zh: 唐兵伐蜀，友謙閱其精兵，命其子令德將以從軍。
units.en: When Tang marched on Shu he mustered his best and sent Lingde to war.
units.literal: When Tang’s army campaigned against Shu, Youqian reviewed his elite troops and ordered his son Lingde to lead them on campaign.

units.zh: 及郭崇韜見殺，伶人景進言：「唐兵初出時，友謙以為討己，閱兵自備。」
units.en: After Guo Chongtao died, the actor Jing Jin said: “When the host first marched, Youqian thought it was for him—he drilled troops and armed.”
units.literal: When Guo Chongtao was killed, the actor Jing Jin said: “When Tang’s army first marched out, Youqian thought it was against him and reviewed troops to arm himself.”

units.zh: 又言：「與崇韜謀反。」
units.en: He also said: “He and Chongtao meant to rebel together.”
units.literal: He also said: “He plotted rebellion with Chongtao.”

units.zh: 且曰：「崇韜所以反於蜀者，以友謙為內應。
units.en: And: “Chongtao turned in Shu because Youqian was his man inside.
units.literal: Moreover he said: “The reason Chongtao rebelled in Shu was that he took Youqian as inner support.

units.zh: 友謙見崇韜死，謀與存乂為郭氏報冤。」
units.en: Seeing Chongtao dead, he plotted with Cunyi to avenge Guo.”
units.literal: When Youqian saw Chongtao dead, he plotted with Cunyi to avenge the Guo clan.”

units.zh: 莊宗初疑其事，群伶、宦官日夜以為言。
units.en: Zhuangzong doubted at first; actors and eunuchs whispered it day and night.
units.literal: Zhuangzong at first doubted the matter; the crowd of actors and eunuchs spoke of it day and night.

units.zh: 友謙聞之大恐，將入朝以自明，將吏皆勸其毋行。
units.en: Youqian heard and was terrified. He meant to go to court and clear his name; officers begged him to stay home.
units.literal: When Youqian heard it he was greatly afraid and was about to enter court to clear himself; his generals and officials all urged him not to go.

units.zh: 友謙曰：「郭公有大功於國，而以讒死，我不自明，誰為我言者！」
units.en: Youqian said: “Guo served the realm and died on lies. If I do not speak for myself, who will?”
units.literal: Youqian said: “Lord Guo rendered great service to the state yet died on slander—if I do not clear myself, who will speak for me!”

units.zh: 乃單車入朝。
units.en: He drove to court alone in one cart.
units.literal: He then came to court alone in a single cart.

units.zh: 景進使人詐為變書，告友謙反。
units.en: Jing Jin forged a dispatch saying Youqian had risen.
units.literal: Jing Jin had men forge a letter of mutiny reporting that Youqian had rebelled.

units.zh: 莊宗惑之，乃徙友謙義成軍節度使，遣朱守殷夜以兵圍其館，驅友謙出徽安門外，殺之，復其姓名。
units.en: Zhuangzong wavered, moved him to Yicheng, and sent Zhu Shouyin at night to ring his lodge. They dragged him past Hui’an Gate and killed him, then took back his old name.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was perplexed, transferred Youqian to military commissioner of Yicheng, sent Zhu Shouyin by night with troops to surround his lodging, drove Youqian out beyond Hui’an Gate, killed him, and restored his former name.

units.zh: 詔魏王繼岌殺令德於遂州，王思同殺令錫於許州，夏魯奇族其家屬於河中。
units.en: An edict ordered Jiji, Prince of Wei, to kill Lingde at Suizhou, Wang Sitong to kill Lingxi at Xu Prefecture, and Xia Luqi to exterminate the rest of the family at Hezhong.
units.literal: An edict ordered Jiji, Prince of Wei, to kill Lingde at Suizhou, Wang Sitong to kill Lingxi at Xu Prefecture, and Xia Luqi to exterminate his household at Hezhong.

units.zh: 魯奇至其家，友謙妻張氏率其宗族二百餘口見魯奇曰：「朱氏宗族當死，願無濫及平人。」
units.en: Luqi came to the house. Lady Zhang led two hundred kin to meet him: “The Zhu line owes death. Spare the servants and strangers.”
units.literal: When Luqi reached the house, Youqian’s wife, Lady Zhang, led more than two hundred of her clan to meet Luqi and said: “The Zhu kindred ought to die; I beg you not to extend the killing to common people.”

units.zh: 乃別其婢仆百人，以其族百口就刑。
units.en: She sent a hundred servants aside; a hundred Zhu went to the block.
units.literal: She then separated out a hundred servant men and maids; the hundred of her clan went to execution.

units.zh: 張氏入室取其鐵券示魯奇曰：「此皇帝所賜也，不知為何語！」
units.en: She went inside, brought out the iron pardon, and held it to Luqi’s face: “The emperor gave this—what language is this?”
units.literal: Lady Zhang entered the room, took out the iron certificate, and showed Luqi, saying: “This was bestowed by the emperor—what do its words mean!”

units.zh: 魯奇亦為之慚。
units.en: Even Luqi flushed.
units.literal: Luqi too was shamed by it.

units.zh: 友謙死，其將史武等七人皆坐友謙族誅，天下冤之。
units.en: When he fell, seven officers including Shi Wu died with the clan for his sake. The realm called it murder.
units.literal: When Youqian died, his generals Shi Wu and six others were all punished by clan extermination for Youqian’s crime; the empire thought it unjust.

units.zh: 袁象先
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian
units.literal: Yuan Xiangxian

units.zh: 袁象先，宋州下邑人，唐南陽王恕己之後也。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian came from Xiayi in Songzhou, descended from Prince Shuji of Nanyang under Tang.
units.literal: Yuan Xiangxian was a native of Xiayi in Songzhou, a descendant of Shuji, Prince of Nanyang under Tang.

units.zh: 父敬初，梁太府卿、駙馬都尉，尚太祖妹，是為萬安大長公主。
units.en: His father Jingchu served Liang as Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury and Commandant of the Horseshoe Escort and married the Founder’s younger sister—the Grand Princess of Wan’an.
units.literal: His father Jingchu was Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury and Commandant of the Horseshoe Escort under Liang; he married a younger sister of the Founder, who was titled Grand Princess of Wan’an.

units.zh: 象先以梁甥為宣武軍內外馬步軍都指揮使，歷宿、洺、陳三州刺史。
units.en: As the Founder’s nephew by marriage, Xiangxian commanded all horse and foot of Xuanwu inside and outside the circuit, then held Suzhou, Mingzhou, and Chenzhou in turn.
units.literal: Xiangxian, as the Founder’s nephew by marriage, became overall commander of horse and foot of the Xuanwu army inside and outside the circuit, and served successively as prefect of Suzhou, Mingzhou, and Chenzhou.

units.zh: 太祖即位，累遷左龍武統軍、在京馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: At the Founder’s accession he rose to Left Dragon Martial Commander and commander of all horse and foot in the capital.
units.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Xiangxian was repeatedly promoted to Left Dragon Martial Commander and overall commander of horse and foot in the capital.

units.zh: 太祖遇弒，友珪立。
units.en: Zhu Wen was murdered; Yougui took the throne.
units.literal: When the Founder was assassinated, Yougui took the throne.

units.zh: 末帝留守東都，以大事謀於趙巖，巖曰：「此事如反掌耳，但得招討楊令公一言諭禁軍，則事可成。」
units.en: The Last Emperor held Luoyang and asked Zhao Yan. Yan said: “This is easy as turning your hand—one word from Yang the Commandant to the forbidden army, and it is done.”
units.literal: The Last Emperor, holding the eastern capital, took counsel on the great affair with Zhao Yan; Yan said: “This affair is like turning one’s palm—only the campaign commissioner Yang the Commandant’s word to instruct the forbidden army, and the deed can succeed.”

units.zh: 末帝即遣人之魏州，以謀告楊師厚，師厚遣裨將王舜賢至洛陽與象先謀，象先許諾。
units.en: He sent to Weizhou; Yang Shihou sent his deputy Wang Shunxian to Luoyang. Xiangxian pledged yes.
units.literal: The Last Emperor then sent men to Weizhou to report the plot to Yang Shihou; Shihou sent his deputy commander Wang Shunxian to Luoyang to plot with Xiangxian; Xiangxian promised.

units.zh: 是時，龍驤軍將劉重遇戍於懷州，以其軍作亂，友珪遣霍彥威擊敗於鄢陵，其餘兵奔散，捕之甚急。
units.en: Liu Chongyu of the Dragon-Prancing Army held Huaizhou and his men rebelled. Yougui sent Huo Yanwei; he broke them at Yanling. Survivors scattered; hunters ran them hard.
units.literal: At that time the Dragon-Prancing Army commander Liu Chongyu was garrisoned at Huaizhou; his troops mutinied; Yougui sent Huo Yanwei to defeat them at Yanling; the rest scattered; pursuit was very tight.

units.zh: 末帝即召龍驤軍在東京者告之曰：「上以重遇故，欲盡召龍驤軍至洛而誅之。」
units.en: The Last Emperor called the Dragon-Prancing men in Luoyang and said: “The throne, because of Chongyu, means to pull every Dragon-Prancing soldier to the capital and kill them all.”
units.literal: The Last Emperor then summoned those of the Dragon-Prancing Army in the eastern capital and told them: “The Emperor above, on account of Chongyu, wishes to summon every man of the Dragon-Prancing Army to Luo and execute them.”

units.zh: 乃偽為友珪詔書示之，龍驤軍恐懼，不知所為，因告之曰：「友珪弒父與君，天下之賊也！
units.en: They forged Yougui’s edict and showed it. The Dragon-Prancing men panicked, helpless, and told them: “Yougui killed his father and his lord—the realm’s bandit!
units.literal: They forged Yougui’s edict and showed it; the Dragon-Prancing Army was afraid and knew not what to do, and therefore told them: “Yougui murdered his father and lord—he is the empire’s bandit!

units.zh: 爾能趨洛陽擒之，以其首祭先帝，則所謂轉禍而為福也。」
units.en: Run to Luoyang, take him, and hang his head before Taizu’s spirit. That is fortune from disaster.”
units.literal: If you can hasten to Luoyang and seize him, offering his head to sacrifice before the late emperor, that is what men call turning misfortune into fortune.”

units.zh: 軍士踴躍曰：「王言是也。」
units.en: The men shouted: “The Prince speaks true.”
units.literal: The soldiers leaped up and said: “The Prince’s words are right.”

units.zh: 末帝即馳奏，言：「龍驤軍反。」
units.en: The Last Emperor galloped word to the throne: “The Dragon Flight Army has risen in revolt.”
units.literal: The Last Emperor at once sent an urgent memorial saying, “The Dragon Flight Army has rebelled.”

units.zh: 象先聞之，即引禁軍千人入宮攻友珪，友珪死。
units.en: Xiangxian heard and led a thousand palace guards straight in to strike Yougui dead.
units.literal: On hearing it, Xiangxian at once led a thousand men of the palace guard into the palace to attack Yougui; Yougui died.

units.zh: 末帝即位，拜象先鎮南軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、開封尹、判在京馬步軍諸軍事。
units.en: The Last Emperor made him military governor of Zhennan, co–Grand Councillor, Kaifeng prefect, and overseer of every horse and foot regiment in the capital.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne he appointed Xiangxian military governor of the Zhennan Army, co–Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, prefect of Kaifeng, and overseer of all horse and foot forces in the capital.

units.zh: 貞明四年，為平盧軍節度使，徙鎮宣武。
units.en: In Zhenming year 4 he took Pinglu, then was moved to Xuanwu.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenming he became military governor of Pinglu and was shifted to govern Xuanwu.

units.zh: 象先為梁將，未嘗有戰功，徒以甥故掌親軍。
units.en: Among Liang generals he had never earned a battle; he commanded the personal guard solely as the emperor’s nephew-in-law.
units.literal: As a Liang general Xiangxian had never won battle merit; he held the personal guard only because he was a nephew by marriage.

units.zh: 及誅友珪，有功於末帝。
units.en: Slaying Yougui was his gift to the Last Emperor.
units.literal: In killing Yougui he had merit toward the Last Emperor.

units.zh: 在宋州十餘年，誅斂其民，積貸千萬。
units.en: More than ten years at Songzhou he bled the people dry and piled loans to the tune of ten million.
units.literal: At Songzhou for more than ten years he extorted and squeezed the people, amassing loans worth tens of millions.

units.zh: 莊宗滅梁，象先來朝洛陽，輦其資數十萬，賂唐將相、伶官、宦者及劉皇后等，由是內外翕然稱其為人。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Liang, Xiangxian came to Luoyang with cartloads of treasure—hundreds of thousands—to buy Tang ministers, actors, eunuchs, Empress Liu. Court and camp alike suddenly called him a fine man.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Xiangxian came to court at Luoyang, carting several hundred thousand in assets to bribe Tang ministers, actors, eunuchs, and Empress Liu and the like; inside and outside alike then praised his character.

units.zh: 莊宗待之甚厚，賜姓名為李紹安，改宣武軍為歸德軍，曰：「歸德之名，為卿設也。」
units.en: Zhuangzong favored him richly, gave him the name Li Shao’an, and renamed Xuanwu the Guide Army: “Guide—that name was made for you.”
units.literal: Zhuangzong treated him very generously, bestowing the surname and personal name Li Shao’an, and changed the Xuanwu army to the Guide army, saying, “The name Guide was made for you.”

units.zh: 遣之還鎮。
units.en: Then sent him back to his post.
units.literal: He sent him back to his command.

units.zh: 是歲卒，年六十，贈太師。
units.en: He died that year at sixty, posthumously Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: That year he died, aged sixty; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 象先二子，正辭官至刺史，泬周世宗時為橫海軍節度使。
units.en: He had two sons—Zhengci reached prefect; Jiao became Henghai military governor under Shizong of Zhou.
units.literal: Xiangxian had two sons: Zhengci rose to prefect; Jiao became military governor of the Henghai army under Later Zhou’s Shizong.

units.zh: 象先平生所積財產數千萬，邸舍四千間，其卒也，不以分諸子，而悉與正辭。
units.en: He had piled tens of millions and four thousand houses. At death he left his sons nothing and gave the whole hoard to Zhengci.
units.literal: The wealth Xiangxian had amassed in his life ran to tens of millions; he owned four thousand lodge-houses. At his death he did not divide it among his sons but gave it all to Zhengci.

units.zh: 正辭初以父任為飛龍副使。
units.en: Zhengci first rode his father’s name into the Soaring Dragon guard as deputy.
units.literal: Zhengci at first held the post of deputy in the Soaring Dragon guard through his father’s influence.

units.zh: 唐廢帝時，獻錢五萬緡，領衢州刺史。
units.en: Under Tang’s deposed emperor he bought Quzhou with fifty thousand strings of cash.
units.literal: Under Tang’s deposed emperor he presented fifty thousand strings of cash and received Quzhou as prefect.

units.zh: 晉高祖入立，復獻五萬緡，求為真刺史。
units.en: When Jin’s Gaozu rose he paid another fifty thousand strings for a real prefecture, not an acting one.
units.literal: When Jin’s Gaozu took the throne he presented another fifty thousand strings and asked for a full prefecture in his own right.

units.zh: 拜雄州刺史，州在靈武之西，吐蕃界中。
units.en: They named him prefect of Xiong—west of Lingwu, deep in the Tibetan marches.
units.literal: He was appointed prefect of Xiongzhou; the prefecture lay west of Lingwu, in Tibetan borderlands.

units.zh: 正辭憚，不欲行，復獻錢數萬，乃得免。
units.en: Zhengci shrank from the posting, paid more cash, and bought his way out.
units.literal: Zhengci was afraid and did not wish to go; he presented several more ten-thousands in cash and was excused.

units.zh: 正辭不勝其忿，以衣帶自經，其家人救之而止。
units.en: Rage choked him; he looped his belt round his neck. Family pulled him down before he finished.
units.literal: Unable to bear his rage, he tried to hang himself with his belt; his household pulled him down in time.

units.zh: 出帝時，又獻錢三萬緡、銀萬兩，出帝憐之，欲與一內郡，未及而卒。
units.en: Under the Deposed Emperor he paid thirty thousand strings and ten thousand taels of silver. The emperor meant to grant him an interior post, but Zhengci died first.
units.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor he again presented thirty thousand strings of cash and ten thousand taels of silver; the Deposed Emperor pitied him and meant to give him an interior commandery, but before he could, Zhengci died.

units.zh: 正辭積錢盈室，室中嘗有聲如牛，人以為妖，勸其散積以禳之。
units.en: Cash packed his rooms until the walls seemed to low like cattle. Neighbors called it a demon and begged him to spend the hoard to quiet it.
units.literal: Zhengci’s hoarded cash filled the rooms; once a sound like an ox was heard within, and people took it for a portent, urging him to scatter the hoard to avert ill luck.

units.zh: 正辭曰：「吾聞物之有聲，求其同類爾，宜益以錢，聲必止。」
units.en: Zhengci said, “When things cry out they are calling their kind. Add more money—the noise will stop.”
units.literal: Zhengci said, “I have heard that when things make a sound they seek their kind; one should add more cash and the sound will surely stop.”

units.zh: 聞者傳以為笑。
units.en: The story passed for a joke across the city.
units.literal: Hearers passed it along as a jest.

units.zh: 朱漢賓
units.en: Zhu Hanbin
units.literal: Zhu Hanbin

units.zh: 朱漢賓，字績臣，亳州譙人也。
units.en: Zhu Hanbin, styled Jichen, came from Qiao in Bozhou.
units.literal: Zhu Hanbin, courtesy name Jichen, was a native of Qiao in Bozhou.

units.zh: 其父元禮為軍校，從梁軍戰，歿於清口。
units.en: His father Yuanli was a camp officer who followed Liang into battle and fell at Qingkou.
units.literal: His father Yuanli was a military officer; he followed the Liang army in battle and died at Qingkou.

units.zh: 漢賓為人有膽力，梁太祖以其父死戰，憐之，以為養子。
units.en: Hanbin had nerve and muscle. Zhu Wen, pitying a boy whose father died in his service, adopted him.
units.literal: Hanbin was a man of courage and force; the Liang Founder, pitying him because his father died in battle, took him as an adopted son.

units.zh: 是時，梁方東攻兗、鄆，鄆州朱瑾募其軍中驍勇者，黥雙雁於其頰，號「雁子都」。
units.en: Liang was driving east on Yan and Yun. Zhu Jin of Yun raised the fiercest fighters, branded twin geese on their cheeks, and called them “Goose Sons.”
units.literal: At that time Liang was attacking east into Yan and Yun; Zhu Jin of Yunzhou recruited the fiercest in his army, tattooed twin wild geese on their cheeks, and called them the “Goose Sons.”

units.zh: 太祖聞之，乃更選勇士數百人，號「落雁都」，以漢賓為指揮使。
units.en: Zhu Wen answered with several hundred picked men, called them “Falling-Goose Company,” and put Hanbin in command.
units.literal: The Founder heard of it and chose several hundred more brave men, called them the “Falling-Goose Company,” and made Hanbin their commander.

units.zh: 及漢賓貴，人猶以為「朱落雁」。
units.en: Even in high office men still called him “Zhu Falling-Goose.”
units.literal: Even after Hanbin grew eminent, people still called him “Zhu Falling-Goose.”

units.zh: 漢賓事梁為天威軍使，歷磁滑宋亳曹五州刺史、安遠軍節度使。
units.en: He commanded the Heavenly Might army, held Ci, Hua, Song, Bo, and Cao in turn, and became military governor of Anyuan.
units.literal: Hanbin served Liang as commander of the Heavenly Might army and in succession held the five prefectures of Ci, Hua, Song, Bo, and Cao, and was military governor of the Anyuan army.

units.zh: 莊宗滅梁，罷漢賓為右龍武統軍，待之頗薄。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Liang he parked Hanbin in the Right Dragon Martial guard and kept him at arm’s length.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he removed Hanbin to commander of the Right Dragon Martial guard and treated him rather coldly.

units.zh: 後莊宗因出遊幸其第，漢賓妻有色而惠，因侍左右，進酒食，奏歌舞，莊宗歡甚，留至夜漏二更而去，漢賓自此有寵。
units.en: Once Zhuangzong called at his house. Hanbin’s wife was lovely and sharp; she poured wine, sang, danced at his side. Zhuangzong stayed till the second watch. After that Hanbin had favor again.
units.literal: Later Zhuangzong on an outing visited his residence; Hanbin’s wife was beautiful and clever, and she waited on him at his side, offering wine and food and performing song and dance. Zhuangzong was greatly pleased, stayed until the second watch of night, and from then Hanbin again had favor.

units.zh: 初，漢賓在梁也，與朱友謙俱為太祖養子，而友謙年長，漢賓以兄事之。
units.en: In Liang days he and Zhu Youqian were both Zhu Wen’s adopted sons; Youqian was senior, and Hanbin treated him as elder brother.
units.literal: Earlier, while still with Liang, Hanbin and Zhu Youqian were both the Founder’s adopted sons; Youqian was the elder, and Hanbin treated him as an elder brother.

units.zh: 其後梁亡，漢賓數寓書友謙，友謙不答，漢賓銜之。
units.en: After Liang fell Hanbin wrote again and again. Youqian never answered. Hanbin brooded on the slight.
units.literal: After Liang fell Hanbin repeatedly sent letters to Youqian; Youqian did not reply, and Hanbin nursed resentment.

units.zh: 其後友謙見族，人皆以為漢賓有力。
units.en: When Youqian’s clan was wiped out, many said Hanbin had helped drive the blade.
units.literal: When Youqian was later exterminated clan-wide, many believed Hanbin had had a hand in it.

units.zh: 明宗入立，以漢賓為莊宗所厚，惡之，以為右衛上將軍。
units.en: Mingzong, who disliked anyone Zhuangzong had loved, made him Right Guard senior general.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he disliked Hanbin for Zhuangzong’s fondness and made him Right Guard senior general.

units.zh: 安重誨用事，漢賓依附之，相為婚姻，由是復得為昭義軍節度使。
units.en: He clung to An Chonghui, married into his house, and won back Zhaoyi as military governor.
units.literal: An Chonghui held power; Hanbin attached himself to him and they became kin by marriage, and so he again became military governor of the Zhaoyi army.

units.zh: 重誨死，漢賓罷為上將軍，遂以太子少保致仕。
units.en: Chonghui died; Hanbin was stripped to senior general, then retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir.
units.literal: When Chonghui died Hanbin was removed to senior general and then retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 漢賓為將，未嘗有戰功，而臨政能守法，好施惠，人頗愛之。
units.en: He never won a battle, but in office he kept the law and gave freely; people liked him for it.
units.literal: As a general Hanbin had never won battle merit, yet in office he could keep the law, loved to show kindness, and the people rather loved him.

units.zh: 清泰二年卒，年六十四。
units.en: He died in Qingtai year 2, aged sixty-four.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he died, aged sixty-four.

units.zh: 晉高祖時，贈太子少傅，謚曰貞惠。
units.en: Jin’s Gaozu posthumously made him Junior Mentor of the Heir with the posthumous name Zhenhui—Loyal and Kind.
units.literal: Under Jin’s Gaozu he was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir and given the posthumous title Zhenhui, “Loyal and Kind.”

units.zh: 段凝，開封人也。
units.en: Duan Ning came from Kaifeng.
units.literal: Duan Ning was a man of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 初名明遠，後更名凝。
units.en: He was born Mingyuan and later took the name Ning.
units.literal: His original name was Mingyuan; later he changed it to Ning.

units.zh: 為澠池主簿。
units.en: He was chief clerk of Mianchi.
units.literal: He served as chief clerk of Mianchi.

units.zh: 其父事梁太祖，以事坐徙。
units.en: His father had served Zhu Wen and was exiled for a fault in office.
units.literal: His father had served the Liang Founder and was banished for an offense in his duties.

units.zh: 後凝棄官，亦事太祖，為軍巡使。
units.en: Ning quit the clerkship and entered Zhu Wen’s service as army patrol commissioner.
units.literal: Later Ning abandoned office and also served the Founder, as army patrol commissioner.

units.zh: 又以其妹內太祖，妹有色，後為美人。
units.en: He placed his younger sister in the Founder’s bed; she was beautiful and rose to palace Beauty.
units.literal: He also gave his younger sister to the Founder; she was beautiful and later became a Beauty of the palace.

units.zh: 凝為人憸巧，善窺迎人意，又以妹故，太祖漸親信之，常使監諸軍。
units.en: Ning was sly and quick to read a man’s mood. The sister won him trust; Zhu Wen often set him to watch the armies.
units.literal: Ning was a man of sly craft, skilled at reading and meeting others’ wishes; because of his sister the Founder gradually trusted him and often had him oversee the armies.

units.zh: 為懷州刺史，梁太祖北征，過懷州，凝獻饋甚豐，太祖大悅。
units.en: They made him prefect of Huai. When Zhu Wen marched north he passed Huai; Ning’s gifts were lavish and the Founder was delighted.
units.literal: He was made prefect of Huai; on the Founder’s northern campaign he passed through Huai, and Ning’s gifts were very rich—the Founder was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 過相州，相州刺史李思安獻饋如常禮，比凝為薄，太祖怒，思安因以得罪死。
units.en: At Xiang, Prefect Li Si’an gave the usual tribute—nothing beside Ning’s feast. Zhu Wen raged; Si’an offended and died for it.
units.literal: Passing Xiangzhou, the Xiang prefect Li Si’an presented gifts according to ordinary ritual—thin compared with Ning’s—and the Founder was angry; Si’an therefore offended and died.

units.zh: 遷凝鄭州刺史，使監兵於河上。
units.en: They moved him to Zhengzhou and set him over the river armies.
units.literal: Ning was moved to Zhengzhou prefect and set to oversee troops on the river.

units.zh: 李振亟請罷之，太祖曰：「凝未有罪。」
units.en: Li Zhen begged to remove him. Zhu Wen said, “Ning has done no crime.”
units.literal: Li Zhen urgently asked that he be removed; the Founder said, “Ning has committed no crime.”

units.zh: 振曰：「待其有罪，則社稷亡矣！」
units.en: Zhen said, “Wait for a crime and the realm will be gone first!”
units.literal: Zhen said, “Wait until he has a crime and the altars of state will already be lost!”

units.zh: 然終不罷也。
units.en: He was never removed.
units.literal: Yet in the end he was not removed.

units.zh: 莊宗已下魏博，與梁相距河上。
units.en: Zhuangzong had taken Weibo; Liang and Tang faced each other across the river.
units.literal: Zhuangzong had already taken Weibo and faced Liang across the river.

units.zh: 梁以王彥章為招討使，凝為副。
units.en: Liang named Wang Yanzhang pacification commissioner and Ning his second.
units.literal: Liang made Wang Yanzhang pacification commissioner and Ning his deputy.

units.zh: 是時，末帝昏亂，小人趙巖、張漢傑等用事，凝依附巖等為奸。
units.en: The Last Emperor was lost; Zhao Yan, Zhang Hanjie, and their kind ruled. Ning rode their coattails into treachery.
units.literal: At that time the Last Emperor was muddled; petty men Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie and the like held power, and Ning clung to Yan and others in wickedness.

units.zh: 彥章為招討使，三日，用奇計破唐德勝南城。
units.en: Yanzhang, as pacification commissioner, took Tang’s southern Desheng citadel in three days with a stratagem.
units.literal: As pacification commissioner Yanzhang, within three days, used a stratagem to take Tang’s southern citadel at Desheng.

units.zh: 而凝與彥章各自上其功，巖等從中匿彥章功狀，悉歸其功於凝。
units.en: Ning and Yanzhang each filed merit. Yan’s clique buried Yanzhang’s report and gave Ning the whole credit.
units.literal: But Ning and Yanzhang each submitted their own merit reports; Yan and the others from the middle suppressed Yanzhang’s account and attributed all merit to Ning.

units.zh: 凝因納金巖等，求代彥章，末帝惑巖等言，卒以凝為招討使，軍於王村。
units.en: Ning bought Yan with gold and asked to replace Yanzhang. The Last Emperor listened; Ning became pacification commissioner at Wangcun.
units.literal: Ning therefore paid gold to Yan and the others and asked to replace Yanzhang; the Last Emperor, swayed by Yan and the rest, finally made Ning pacification commissioner, with the army at Wangcun.

units.zh: 是時，唐已下鄆州，凝乃自酸棗決河東註鄆，以隔絕唐軍，號「護駕水」。
units.en: Tang had Yun. Ning cut the Yellow River east from Suanzao to flood toward Yun and wall off Tang’s host, calling it the “Imperial-Guard Water.”
units.literal: By then Tang had taken Yunzhou; Ning cut the Yellow River east from Suanzao to flood toward Yun and cut off the Tang army, calling it the “Imperial-Guard Water.”

units.zh: 莊宗自鄆趨汴，汴兵悉已屬凝，京師無備，乃遣張漢倫馳驲召凝於河上，漢倫中道墜馬，傷不能進。
units.en: Zhuangzong ran from Yun on Bian. Every soldier at Bian answered to Ning; the capital was bare. They sent Zhang Hanlun by relay to pull Ning off the river—Hanlun fell midway and could not ride on.
units.literal: Zhuangzong raced from Yun toward Bian; all Bian’s troops were already under Ning, and the capital was undefended, so they sent Zhang Hanlun by relay horse to summon Ning from the river—but Hanlun fell from his horse midway and was too injured to go on.

units.zh: 已而梁亡，凝率精兵五萬降唐，莊宗賜以錦袍、御馬。
units.en: Liang fell. Ning brought fifty thousand elite horse to Tang. Zhuangzong gave brocade and an imperial mount.
units.literal: Soon Liang fell; Ning led fifty thousand elite troops to surrender to Tang, and Zhuangzong gave him brocade robes and an imperial horse.

units.zh: 明日，凝奏：「故梁奸人趙巖、張漢傑等十餘人侮弄權柄，殘害生靈，請皆族之。」
units.en: Next day he memorialized: “Liang’s villains Zhao Yan, Zhang Hanjie, and a dozen more played with power and ruined the people—exterminate every clan.”
units.literal: The next day Ning memorialized, “The former Liang villains Zhao Yan, Zhang Hanjie, and more than ten others toyed with power and harmed the living; I ask that their clans all be exterminated.”

units.zh: 凝出入唐朝無隗色，見唐將相若倡優，因伶人景進納賂劉皇后，以求恩寵。
units.en: He walked Tang’s halls without shame, treating ministers like players. Through the actor Jing Jin he bought Empress Liu’s favor.
units.literal: Ning moved through Tang court without shame, treating Tang ministers like actors; through the actor Jing Jin he paid bribes to Empress Liu to seek favor.

units.zh: 莊宗甚親愛之，賜姓名曰李紹欽，以為泰寧軍節度使。
units.en: Zhuangzong doted on him, gave him the name Li Shaoqin, and made him military governor of Taining.
units.literal: Zhuangzong cherished him greatly, bestowed the surname and name Li Shaoqin, and made him military governor of the Taining army.

units.zh: 居月餘，用庫錢數十萬，有司請責其償，莊宗釋之。
units.en: In a month he burned through hundreds of thousands from the treasury. The accountants demanded repayment. Zhuangzong let it go.
units.literal: Within a little over a month he spent several hundred thousand from the treasury; the relevant office asked that he make restitution, and Zhuangzong released him.

units.zh: 郭崇韜固請，以為不可，莊宗怒曰：「朕為卿所制，都不自由！」
units.en: Guo Chongtao insisted it could not stand. Zhuangzong snapped, “You rule me—I am not free!”
units.literal: Guo Chongtao pressed hard that it could not be done; Zhuangzong raged, “I am controlled by you and have no freedom at all!”

units.zh: 終釋之。
units.en: In the end he released him anyway.
units.literal: In the end he released him.

units.zh: 莊宗遣李紹宏監諸將備契丹，凝軍瓦橋關，以諂事紹宏，紹宏數薦凝可大用，郭崇韜每以為不可。
units.en: Zhuangzong sent Li Shaohong to watch the generals against the Khitan. Ning held Waqiao Pass and flattered him; Shaohong kept pushing Ning for high office, and Guo Chongtao kept saying no.
units.literal: Zhuangzong sent Li Shaohong to oversee the generals against the Khitan; Ning’s army was at Waqiao Pass, and he flattered Shaohong, who repeatedly recommended Ning for great appointment, while Guo Chongtao always objected.

units.zh: 遷武勝軍節度使。
units.en: They moved him to military governor of Wusheng.
units.literal: He was moved to military governor of the Wusheng army.

units.zh: 趙在禮反，紹宏請以凝招討，莊宗使凝條奏方略，凝所請偏裨，皆其故黨，莊宗疑之，乃止。
units.en: When Zhao Zaili rose, Shaohong wanted Ning as pacifier. Zhuangzong asked his plan; every deputy Ning named was an old crony. Zhuangzong smelled a plot and stopped.
units.literal: When Zhao Zaili rebelled, Shaohong asked that Ning be made pacification commissioner; Zhuangzong had Ning lay out a plan, but every deputy Ning requested was an old crony, and Zhuangzong grew suspicious and stopped.

units.zh: 明宗即位，勒歸田里。
units.en: Mingzong’s accession sent him home to his village.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he compelled him to return to his home village.

units.zh: 明年，長流遼州，賜死。
units.en: Next year they exiled him to distant Liaozhou and granted death.
units.literal: The next year he was exiled far to Liaozhou and granted death.

units.zh: 劉玘
units.en: Liu Qi
units.literal: Liu Qi

units.zh: 劉玘，汴州雍丘人也，世為宣武軍牙將。
units.en: Liu Qi came from Yongqiu in Bianzhou; his family had served for generations as Xuanwu army guard officers.
units.literal: Liu Qi was a native of Yongqiu in Bianzhou; for generations his family had served as Xuanwu army guard officers.

units.zh: 梁太祖鎮宣武，玘以軍卒補隊長，稍以戰功遷牙將，為襄州都指揮使。
units.en: When Zhu Wen held Xuanwu, Qi entered as a rank soldier and became squad leader; battle by battle he rose to guard officer and overall commander of Xiangzhou.
units.literal: When the Liang Founder held Xuanwu, Qi entered as a rank soldier and was made squad leader; gradually through battle merit he was promoted to guard officer and made overall commander of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 山南節度使王班為亂軍所殺，亂軍推玘為留後，玘偽許之，明日饗士于庭，伏甲幕中，酒半，擒為亂者殺之。
units.en: Shannan governor Wang Ban fell to mutineers who wanted Qi as acting commissioner. Qi pretended yes; next day he feasted the men in the courtyard with armored troops hidden behind the screens, and at mid-feast seized and killed the ringleaders.
units.literal: Shannan military governor Wang Ban was killed by mutineers; they pushed Qi as acting commissioner. Qi feigned assent; the next day he feasted the troops in the courtyard and hid armored men behind the screens; at mid-feast he seized and killed the ringleaders.

units.zh: 會梁遣陳暉兵亦至，襄州平，以功拜復州刺史，徙亳、安二州。
units.en: Chen Hui’s Liang troops arrived too; Xiangzhou was pacified. Qi was made prefect of Fuzhou, then moved through Bozhou and Anzhou.
units.literal: When Liang also sent Chen Hui’s troops, Xiangzhou was pacified; for the merit he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou and was moved through Bozhou and Anzhou.

units.zh: 末帝時，為晉州觀察留後，凡八年，日與晉人交戰。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor he held Jinzhou as observation commissioner for eight years, battling Jin every day.
units.literal: Under the Last Emperor he was observation commissioner at Jinzhou for eight years, fighting Jin forces day after day.

units.zh: 莊宗滅梁，玘來朝，莊宗勞之曰：「劉侯亡恙，爾居晉陽之南鄙久矣，不早相聞，今日見訪，不其晚邪？」
units.en: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Qi came to court. Zhuangzong greeted him: “Lord Liu, are you well? You have long held the southern marches beyond Taiyuan. Why no word until now? To call only today—is that not late?”
units.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Qi came to court. Zhuangzong consoled him, saying: “Lord Liu, are you well? You have long held the southern marches beyond Taiyuan. Why did you not report sooner? To visit only today—is it not late?”

units.zh: 玘頓首謝罪，遣還鎮，遂以為節度使，徙鎮安遠。
units.en: Qi kowtowed and begged pardon; Zhuangzong sent him back, then made him military governor and moved him to Anyuan.
units.literal: Qi prostrated himself and begged pardon; Zhuangzong sent him back to his post, then made him military governor and moved him to govern Anyuan.

units.zh: 天成元年，以史敬鎔代之，玘還京師，未至，拜武勝軍節度使，以疾卒于道中，贈侍中。
units.en: In Tiancheng year 1, Shi Jingrong replaced him. Qi headed for the capital; before he arrived they made him military governor of Wusheng, but he died of illness on the road and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, Shi Jingrong replaced him; Qi started back to the capital, and before arriving was appointed military governor of the Wusheng army, but died of illness on the road and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 周知裕
units.en: Zhou Zhiyu
units.literal: Zhou Zhiyu

units.zh: 周知裕，字好問，幽州人也。
units.en: Zhou Zhiyu, styled Haowen, came from Youzhou.
units.literal: Zhou Zhiyu, courtesy name Haowen, was a man of Youzhou.

units.zh: 為劉仁恭騎將，仁恭為其子守光所囚，知裕去事守光兄守文。
units.en: He rode for Liu Rengong until Rengong’s son Shouguang imprisoned him; Zhiyu then served the elder brother Shouwen.
units.literal: He was a cavalry officer under Liu Rengong; Rengong was imprisoned by his son Shouguang, and Zhiyu left to serve Shouguang’s elder brother Shouwen.

units.zh: 守光又攻殺守文，乃與張萬進立守文子延祚而事之。
units.en: Shouguang killed Shouwen too. Zhiyu and Zhang Wanjin set up Shouwen’s son Yanzuo and served him.
units.literal: Shouguang again attacked and killed Shouwen; he and Zhang Wanjin then set up Shouwen’s son Yanzuo and served him.

units.zh: 守光又殺廷祚，以其子繼威代之。
units.en: Shouguang killed Yanzuo as well and put his own son Jiewei in his place.
units.literal: Shouguang also killed Yanzuo and replaced him with his own son Jiewei.

units.zh: 萬進殺繼威，與知裕俱奔於梁。
units.en: Wanjin killed Jiewei; he and Zhiyu fled together to Liang.
units.literal: Wanjin killed Jiewei; he and Zhiyu both fled to Liang.

units.zh: 梁太祖得知裕喜甚，為置歸化軍，以知裕為指揮使，凡與晉戰所得，及兵背晉而歸梁者，皆以隸知裕。
units.en: Zhu Wen was overjoyed. He formed the Return-to-Righteousness army under Zhiyu and dumped into it every prisoner from Jin wars and every deserter from Jin.
units.literal: The Liang Founder was delighted to gain Zhiyu, established for him the Return-to-Righteousness army, made Zhiyu its commander, and assigned to him everyone taken in battle against Jin and every soldier who left Jin for Liang.

units.zh: 梁、晉相拒河上十餘年，其摧堅陷陣，歸化一軍為最，然知裕位不過刺史。
units.en: For ten years Liang and Jin fought on the river; no unit broke lines like Return-to-Righteousness—yet Zhiyu never rose above prefect.
units.literal: Liang and Jin faced each other on the river more than ten years; for storming strongpoints and breaking lines the Return-to-Righteousness army was foremost, yet Zhiyu’s rank never rose above prefect.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，知裕與段凝軍河上，聞梁已亡，欲自殺，為賓客故人止之，乃降唐。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Zhiyu and Duan Ning were on the river. Hearing Liang was gone he meant to die; friends held him back and he surrendered to Tang.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Zhiyu and Duan Ning were with the army on the river; hearing Liang had fallen, he wished to kill himself, but guests and old friends stopped him, and he surrendered to Tang.

units.zh: 莊宗尤寵待之，諸將嫉其寵，因獵射之，知裕走以免。
units.en: Zhuangzong spoiled him. Jealous generals shot at him on a hunt; Zhiyu ran clear.
units.literal: Zhuangzong favored him especially; the other generals resented his favor, and on a hunt they shot at him—Zhiyu ran and escaped.

units.zh: 莊宗為殺射者，以知裕為房州刺史。
units.en: Zhuangzong killed the shooters and made him prefect of Fang.
units.literal: Zhuangzong executed the shooters and made Zhiyu prefect of Fang.

units.zh: 明宗時，歷絳、淄二州刺史，遷宿州團練使、安州留後。
units.en: Under Mingzong he held Jiang and Zi, then Suzhou as Tuanlian commissioner and An as acting prefect.
units.literal: Under Mingzong he in succession held Jiang and Zi as prefect, then became Tuanlian commissioner of Suzhou and acting prefect of An.

units.zh: 所居皆有善政。
units.en: Every post he held was well governed.
units.literal: Wherever he served he had good government.

units.zh: 安州近淮，俗惡病者，父母有疾，置之佗室，以竹竿系飲食委之，至死不近。
units.en: An lay on the Huai. Locals feared the sick: parents with illness were shut in another room; food came down on bamboo poles; no one approached till death.
units.literal: An lay near the Huai; the custom hated the sick—when parents fell ill they were put in another room, food and drink lowered in on bamboo poles, and no one came near until death.

units.zh: 知裕深患之，加以教道，由是稍革。
units.en: Zhiyu hated the custom and taught against it until the practice slowly died.
units.literal: Zhiyu was deeply troubled by this and added instruction and guidance, and the custom was gradually reformed.

units.zh: 罷為右神武統軍。
units.en: They moved him to commander of the Right Divine Martial guard.
units.literal: He was removed to commander of the Right Divine Martial guard.

units.zh: 應順中卒，贈太傅。
units.en: He died in the Yingshun reign and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
units.literal: He died in the Yingshun era and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 陸思鐸
units.en: Lu Siduo
units.literal: Lu Siduo

units.zh: 陸思鐸，澶州臨黃人也。
units.en: Lu Siduo was from Linhuang in Chan Prefecture.
units.literal: Lu Siduo was a native of Linhuang in Chan Prefecture.

units.zh: 少事梁為宣武軍卒，以善射知名。
units.en: Young he soldiered in the Xuanwu army and was famed for the bow.
units.literal: In youth he served Liang as a soldier of the Xuanwu army and was known for skill in archery.

units.zh: 累遷拱辰左廂都指揮使，領恩州刺史。
units.en: He rose to left-wing commander of the Bowmen of the Constellation and held En as prefect.
units.literal: He rose to commander of the left wing of the Bowmen of the Constellation guard and held En prefecture.

units.zh: 梁、晉相拒河上，思鐸鏤其姓名於箭筈以射晉軍，而矢中莊宗馬鞍，莊宗拔矢，見思鐸姓名，奇之。
units.en: On the river he carved his name on arrow shafts and shot at Jin. One struck Zhuangzong’s saddle; Zhuangzong drew it, read Siduo’s name, and marveled.
units.literal: While Liang and Jin faced each other on the river, Siduo engraved his name on arrow shafts and shot at the Jin army; a shaft struck Zhuangzong’s saddle, and Zhuangzong pulled the arrow, saw Siduo’s name, and marveled.

units.zh: 其後滅梁，思鐸謁見，莊宗出其矢以示之，思鐸伏地請死，莊宗慰而起之，拜龍武右廂都指揮使。
units.en: After Liang fell Siduo came to court. Zhuangzong showed the arrow. Siduo kowtowed for death; Zhuangzong lifted him and made him right-wing commander of the Dragon Martial guard.
units.literal: After Liang was destroyed Siduo came to audience; Zhuangzong produced the arrow to show him. Siduo prostrated himself and asked for death; Zhuangzong comforted him and raised him, appointing him commander of the right wing of the Dragon Martial guard.

units.zh: 晉高祖時，為陳、蔡二州刺史。
units.en: Under Jin’s Gaozu he held Chen and Cai as prefect.
units.literal: Under Jin’s Gaozu he was prefect of Chen and Cai.

units.zh: 卒年五十四。
units.en: He died at fifty-four.
units.literal: He died aged fifty-four.

units.zh: 思鐸在陳州，有善政，臨終戒其子曰：「陳人愛我，我死則葬焉。」
units.en: Siduo held Chenzhou and ruled kindly. Dying, he told his son: “The people of Chen love me. When I am gone, bury me here.”
units.literal: Siduo was at Chenzhou and had good governance; on his deathbed he admonished his son, saying: “The people of Chen love me—when I die, bury me there.”

units.zh: 遂葬於陳州。
units.en: So they buried him at Chenzhou.
units.literal: He was thereupon buried at Chenzhou.
